title: LLMs with in-context learning for Algorithmic Theoretical Physics
version: arXiv:2605.08212v1, submitted 2026-05-06; report number IPMU26-0020; license CC BY 4.0
locator: Full HTML (arxiv.org/html/2605.08212v1): Sec. 3.2 implementation, Sec. 3.4 evaluation rules, Sec. 3.5 contexts, Sec. 4 results and failure discussions, Sec. 5 conclusions, reference list
relevance: Closest public measurement of a single LLM agent with a computer-algebra runtime on novel research-grade problems; its documented failure modes and stage-wise pass/fail rubric are directly reusable for our audit design.
limits: Single model (Claude Opus 4-6), single CAS (Maple), 9 problems in one problem family (cosmological perturbation dof counts). Each problem run once; authors say behavior is 'relatively stable' but report no variance estimate. No public code repository named in the paper text read here.
setup: Claude Opus 4-6 via API driving a Maple REPL (prettyprint=0), max_tokens=1024, thinking off for main runs, 100-turn cap, expert-written contexts. Problems passed as plain text.
quantitative_results: Pass rates by context: 10ex (10 worked examples, 60k tokens) 5/9; 3broad (3 examples, 18k) 5/9; 3tailored (3 examples retargeted at observed failure modes, 24k) 7/9; instruction (2k recipe, no code) 3/9. More turns and Maple restarts correlate with failure. Thinking tokens: little improvement in the five spot-checked runs.
failure_modes_documented: Misinterpretation of problem conventions: 'flat background' read as flat FLRW rather than Minkowski in several problems across contexts (Sec. 4.2, 4.4).
Task abandonment driven by perceived triviality: sRMs solved then abandoned to 'generalize' it, failing (Sec. 4.1).
Incorrect order reduction of higher derivatives when Lagrange-multiplier constraints are forgotten (sRFs, sRi2Fs, sRi2Ft; Sec. 4.1).
Unflagged conditional equivalence: a rewritten action used for sRFs is equivalent only if f''(chi) != 0, used without stating the condition (Sec. 4.2).
Silent branch choice among multiple background solutions (noted across problems; Sec. 4.1).

Unprompted use of training-set knowledge: Starobinsky problem solved by introducing an external scalar via a known trick despite a Jordan-frame restriction (Sec. 4.1); in context 3tailored it followed the required route.
Decision paralysis and minimal tool use with instruction-only context (Sec. 4.4); stuck sessions restart the CAS (up to 7 restarts).
evaluation_rubric: Expert pass/fail per staged solution: (1) wrong setup = fail; (2) background equations not substituted is a fail only if it affects the result; (3) perturbations and derivative reduction must be correct; (4) a correct final result with a forgotten subtlety still passes (Sec. 3.4).
reusable_artifacts: Context-design recipe: worked examples beat abstract recipes; a small representative set beats a large one; retarget examples at observed failure modes (Sec. 5.2-5.3, Appendix B recipe).
Stage-wise grading rubric (Sec. 3.4) transferable to any staged derivation.
Turn/restart counts as cheap difficulty telemetry (Fig. 2).
authors_claim: Authors evaluate ability 'on par with a first-year graduate student' for this problem family; they explicitly do not claim autonomous physics discovery.
proof_status: Empirical evaluation, not a proof; results are the authors' expert gradings.
dependencies: Claude Opus 4-6 API; Maple runtime; no other tooling described.
open_questions: Would failure classes transfer to a proof-assistant setting or to the project's Lean-based checks?
No variance across repeated runs; reruns and other models untested in the paper.

title: Multi-agent Autoformalization of Tensor Network Theory
locator: Main text ('Catching unintended formalizations', 'Discussion'); Supplementary appendices as in HTML v1: A.1 agent-role table, A.2 delegation, C persistent memory, D.1-D.3 orchestration patterns, E paper-to-formalization gap analysis, F cost, H agent definitions
relevance: The most complete public multi-agent autoformalization workflow for theoretical physics; its roles, blueprint discipline, gap taxonomy, and stated bottleneck (enforcing mathematical intent) are the primary design inputs for our extraction/translation/counterexample/review roles.
limits: Authors' report of their own run; Lean build and review reports not independently rebuilt here (repository inspected at discovery depth only, see meth-tnlean-repo). Costs are the authors' recorded API totals. Formal target is mathematical physics (FT-MPS), not interpretive physics arguments.

workflow_design.roles: leanOrchestrator (expensive tier; decomposition, dispatch, repo access), lean (expensive; proof writing), leanSearch (inexpensive; Mathlib scouting, web/arXiv lookup), leanSimplifier (inexpensive; style and simplification), leanBlueprint (inexpensive; blueprint-Lean sync, bibliography), reviewer (inexpensive; runs on proposed repository changes). Roles were introduced incrementally as bottlenecks appeared (App. A.1).
workflow_design.delegation: Sub-agents run in isolation with fixed role, task instructions, background notes, assigned edit files, and model tier; parallel agents get disjoint file sets (App. A.2, D.1).
orchestration_patterns: Parallel dispatch of 3-5 sub-agents on disjoint file sets, merged and full-built by the orchestrator (D.1).
Scout-then-prove: an inexpensive scout writes a design memo with exact theorem signatures to persistent memory; the expensive prover receives it as read-only context (D.2).
Review-repair cycles converging in 2-3 rounds, with a safety cap of five iterations and no fresh review on each revision to avoid unbounded loops (D.3).
workflow_design.memory: 453 memory files recording tried routes, false statements with counterexamples, and conventions; distilled, project-independent files released under docs/audits/ and docs/paper-gaps/ (App. C).
workflow_design.artifacts: Blueprint (leanblueprint) linking prose statements to Lean declarations via \lean/\leanok tags checked by checkdecls; paper-gap notes published where formal statements diverge from sources.

failure_modes_documented: Weakened statement: agents proved FT-MPS under an extra 'doubly stochastic' gauge (transfer operator both unital and trace-preserving), formally correct but valid for a much smaller tensor class; expensive to remove because later lemmas depended on it (main text 'Weakening of the theorem').

Finite/asymptotic substitution: finite-N statement replaced by an asymptotic norm comparison with wrong hypotheses; agents could not self-patch; humans pointed at the flawed definition (main text 'Finite vs asymptotic limit').
Vacuous statements: proving from hypotheses never satisfied (main text 'Catching unintended formalizations', first paragraph).
Edge cases: absent D>=1, N>=1 assumptions forced Lean through nonphysical cases D=0, N=0 (main text 'Edge cases').
Blueprint-code drift: correct Lean with drifted prose; fixed by explicit synchronization and review criteria (main text 'Lean code-Blueprint alignment').

Resource limits: heartbeat-bounded proofs (default 200,000); factoring a proof cut one from 1,600,000 to 250,000 heartbeats; stale diagnostics need server restart; scouted lemmas can have mismatched types unless inspected (App. D.2).
quantitative_results: Core development ~62,000 lines, 2,300 declarations, 233 files inside a ~227,000-line library; six blueprint review rounds for FT-MPS; recorded model-API cost $20,206 whole library, estimated $5,548 for FT-MPS (App. F). Agents found a nonstandard proof of the injective case via Skolem-Noether autonomously (main text).
authors_claim: 'We find that the main bottleneck in large-scale autoformalization is enforcing mathematical intent' (abstract); human intervention is strategic (which statement is intended), not tactical (how to prove it).
proof_status: Authors report a sorry-free FT-MPS core argument machine-checked in Lean; not rebuilt in this audit.
dependencies: Lean 4, Mathlib, TeXRA agent platform; QICLean companion library (per repository README).
open_questions: Do the reviewer prompts released with TNLean catch the defect classes our pilot injects (weakening, vacuity, untraceable premises)?
How much of the role/tool design transfers to non-Lean, interpretive physics comparison tasks where no kernel exists?

title: Axioms for physical reasoning: codifying the Seiberg-Witten solution in Lean
version: arXiv:2607.06379v1, submitted 2026-07-07; companion repository mrdouglasny/seiberg-witten (not inspected in this pass)
locator: HTML v1: Sec. 2 two kinds of formalization; Sec. 4.1 dictionary; Sec. 4.2 H0-H7; Sec. 4.4 what formalizing forces into the open; Sec. 5 checking the axioms; Appendices A-B
relevance: The clearest public discipline for separating named physical postulates from checked mathematics, with a working semantic-audit practice: dependency printing, numerical oracle, adversarial statement review, and vacuity hardening. Direct template for our audit procedure.
limits: Authors' report; repository and oracle scripts not inspected or rerun here. The physical postulates are argued for, not derived; their justification is external review plus numerics by the authors' own account.
design_principles: Physical postulates are named predicates carried in theorem types (H0-H7); the Lean `axiom` keyword carries only mathematics, so physics never hides in the trusted base (Sec. 2, 4.2, Appendix A).

A single dictionary maps each physical concept to a named mathematical object (e.g., PeriodChart.a/.aD/.tau as coupling; SymplecticReframing as duality); physics enters only through the dictionary (Sec. 4.1).
#print axioms reports the complete trusted base of any result; the genus-one uniqueness theorem's reported footprint is three logical axioms plus two classical covering axioms (Sec. 4.3).
Two kinds of formalization distinguished: proving existing rigorous statements vs. codifying trusted non-rigorous arguments (Sec. 2).
failure_modes_documented: Vacuous hypotheses: first-pass H3 ('there exists a lattice map equal to the Picard-Lefschetz transvection') was true by fiat; hardened to demand an actual deck transformation with covariant central charge. H2 hardened to demand a nonzero charge go massless; H5 pinned to 'exactly 2N' was unsatisfiable at rank 1 and corrected to 'order dividing 2N' with the u -> -u reflection as witness (Sec. 4.4).
A convenient falsehood refused by types: single-valued periods would be vacuous (bounded holomorphic map extends and is constant); data must live on the universal cover (Sec. 4.4).

Family-dependence trap: H6's instanton expansion with free coefficients fits any prepotential at fixed Lambda; content appears only as a weighted-homogeneity clause across the Lambda-family (Sec. 4.4). Heuristic recorded: for every existential inside a hypothesis, ask what stops the witness being reverse-engineered.

Adversarial review beat 62 passing numerical checks: a proposed axiom set failed statement-level review with three gaps (pointwise existence without holomorphic choice, missing boundary limits, an unlabelled parabolic slot); a hyperbolic matrix briefly occupied a parabolic slot passing every property the proofs consumed (Sec. 5, 'Validating a transcription').

The checking apparatus itself erred twice (fractional power on the wrong branch; cycle normalization off by a factor of two), caught by anchor values such as lambda(i)=1/2 before agreeing with Lean (Sec. 5, oracle paragraph).
verification_protocol_as_published: Cheapest first: (1) independent numerical oracle in mpmath/numpy sharing no code or authorship with Lean - 9 suites, 278 checks at 30-40 digit precision; authors call a numerical pass 'necessary, not sufficient'; (2) cross-model and self-review against pinned sources, separating 'is it proved?', 'does it say what the source says?', and 'can the intended theorems be derived from it?'; (3) transcription validation with four checks - instantiation, oracle, agreement with independently proved results, adversarial content; (4) the physicist's triangle: independent routes to the same quantity (perturbation theory, Nekrasov instantons, exact periods) attached as a cross-check rather than asserted (Sec. 5).
authors_claim: AI's characteristic error in physics derivations is 'a hallucinated assumption, an unphysical premise or a dropped subtlety presented as if derived' (Sec. 1) - the error class our audit targets.
proof_status: Authors report sorry-free genus-one theorems with printed axiom footprints; not rebuilt here.
open_questions: Inspect mrdouglasny/seiberg-witten: pin commit, read validate_singcount.py and oracle suites, verify the printed axiom footprints by building.

title: AxQM: A Textbook-Scale Benchmark for Formal Proof Synthesis in a Library of Finite-Dimensional Quantum Mechanics
relevance: Largest public kernel-graded physics proof-synthesis benchmark; its grading is exactly the boundary case for our design: kernel checking verifies compilation, no sorry, no new axioms - and not statement-level correspondence, which is the gap our semantic audit addresses.
limits: Abstract-level in this pass; repository previously inspected at discovery depth by the kb-formalization lane (form-axqm): public benchmark statements carry intentional sorries; solutions private.
authors_claim: Tasks derive from a near-complete formalization of the formal portions of Nielsen-Chuang, so every task is guaranteed a solution; grading is deterministic via the Lean kernel (compiles, no sorry in dependency closure, no new axioms).
open_questions: Do any AxQM tasks cover clock/conditioning statements usable as known-answer items for our pilot, and does the private-solutions policy permit external auditing?

title: Agentic Diagrammatica: Towards Autonomous Symbolic Computation in High Energy Physics

authors_claim: Concentrating the agent's action distribution onto convention-fixing tool calls validated on an exhaustive known-answer catalog (all tree-level 1->2 single-vertex partial widths with massless and threshold limits) plus an NDA case study.
proof_status: Authors' validation claim; not reproduced here.
